1243:
This Chapter shall be known and may be cited as the "Pedestrian and Vehicle Safety Ordinance of Glynn County".
(Ord. No. O-2023-07, § I, 6/1/2023)
1244:
This ordinance regulates the time, place, and manner of pedestrians and drivers in right-of-way and shall not apply to anyone exercising their rights to constitutionally-protected activity.
(Ord. No. O-2023-07, § I, 6/1/2023)
1245:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this Ordinance, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning. When not inconsistent with the context, words in the plural number include the singular number, and words in the singular include the plural number.
Approach shall mean to move nearer in distance to someone.
Designated roadways shall mean the interstate/intrastate system (including interstate/intrastate entrance and exit ramps and any Georgia Department of Transportation right-of-way), and arterial and collector roadways and rights-of-way. For purposes of this definition, collector and arterial roadways and rights-of-way shall be those roadways (and their rights-of-way) classified as a collector or higher in the Subdivision Regulations of Glynn County, Georgia. This definition also encompasses the first 450 feet of local roadways intersecting with these designated roadways and any areas within the rights-of-way not designated or intended for pedestrian use.
The portions of these designated roadways subject to this Chapter include the portions within the area open for vehicular traffic (including medians), plus four feet outside of the shoulders and/or curbs.
Legally parked shall mean a vehicle that is standing, stopped, or parked m an area designated, or legally authorized, for parking.
The traveled portion of a designated roadway shall mean any portion of a designated roadway (including travel lanes, turn lanes, bike lanes and shoulders) that is normally used by moving motor vehicle traffic that is not an area designated for or routinely used as a parking area for the general public.
Median shall mean any area separating traffic lanes on a roadway. A median includes, but is not limited to, any paved or unpaved, marked or unmarked, landscaped or non-landscaped, portions of a roadway which exist between lanes of traffic.
Public rights-of-way shall mean land, property or interest therein, usually but not required to be a strip, acquired for or devoted to a county road, sidewalk, curb, gutter, drainage inlet, manhole or water valve.
Ordinance shall mean the Pedestrian and Vehicle Safety Ordinance of Glynn County and any portion thereof.
(Ord. No. O-2023-07, § I, 6/1/2023)
1246:
Except as provided herein, it shall be unlawful for any person in the unincorporated areas of Glynn County, excluding Jekyll Island, to make use of the public rights-of-way in a manner that interferes with the safe and efficient movement of people and property from place to place on a public road or right-of-way. Unless otherwise authorized by Glynn County, it shall be unlawful for any person in the unincorporated areas of Glynn County, excluding Jekyll Island, to commit any of the following acts:
(a) Occupancy of median. It is unlawful for any person to stop, stand, or otherwise occupy or remain in a median on any designated roadway when that person is not in the process of lawfully crossing the road in accordance with applicable traffic and safety laws. Stopping, standing, or otherwise occupying a median through two consecutive opportunities to cross in accordance with applicable traffic and safety laws is prima facie evidence of a violation of this Subsection.
(b) Physical interaction on roadway. It is unlawful for any person to engage in any physical interaction between a pedestrian and an occupant of a motor vehicle, including but not limited to the transfer of any product or material, while the motor vehicle is not legally parked and is located on the traveled portion of a designated roadway.
(c) Commercial use of public rights-of-way. It is unlawful to use any public right-of-way for commercial activity. Commercial activity prohibited by this Section includes, but is not limited to, vending or sale of goods, display of goods for sale, storage of goods for sale in connection with commercial activity, or repair or manufacturing of goods. Signage is not "commercial activity" regulated by this Chapter; however, there shall be no signage placed or displayed in any median. Use of a vehicle to transport goods and services is not "commercial activity" regulated by this Chapter.
(d) Activities on private property. It is unlawful for any person to knowingly approach another person, unless such other person consents, for the purpose of passing any material, item or object to, displaying a sign to, or requesting any material, item or object from such other person on private property if the owner, tenant, or lawful occupant has asked the person not to enter the property, or has posted a sign clearly indicating that approaches are not welcome on the property.
(e) Activities in certain areas. It is unlawful for any person to knowingly approach another person within six feet of such person, unless such other person consents, for the purpose of passing any material, item or object to, displaying a sign to, or requesting any material, item or object from such other person in the public right-of-way within a radius of 30 feet from:
(1) Any bus stop;
(2) The entrance or exit of any public toilet facility; or
(3) An automatic teller machine (ATM), provided that when an ATM is located within an ATM facility, such distance shall be measured from the entrance or exit of the ATM facility.
(Ord. No. O-2023-07, § I, 6/1/2023)
1248:
(a) The Chief of Police shall implement, administer and enforce the provisions of this Ordinance.
(b) Each and every day a violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense. Each and every violation of this Ordinance, including separate violations on the same day, shall be deemed a separate offense.
(c) For the first violation of this Ordinance, the Chief of Police or his or her designee shall issue a warning to the person in violation, and shall document the issuance of the warning.
(d) After receiving a warning pursuant to Section 2-33-6(c) hereof, any person in violation of this Ordinance, upon conviction, shall be guilty of an ordinance violation punishable by a fine of at least $100.00, but not to exceed $1,000.00; or by imprisonment of at least 24 hours, not to exceed 60 days; or both. Any person who violates this Ordinance may be subject to immediate arrest.
(Ord. No. O-2023-07, § I, 6/1/2023)
1250:
This Article regulates the time, place, and manner of solicitations in the unincorporated areas of Glynn County, Georgia, and shall not apply to anyone exercising their rights to constitutionally-protected activity.
(Ord. No. O-2024-03, § II, 3/21/2024)
1251:
The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this Article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning. When not inconsistent with the context, words in the plural number include the singular number, and words in the singular number include the plural number.
Solicit or solicitation shall mean to request an immediate donation of money or other thing of value from another person, regardless of the solicitor's purpose or intended use of the money or other thing of value, including a request for employment, business, or contributions, or to request the sale of goods or services under circumstances where a reasonable person would understand that the purchase of the goods or services is a donation. This definition shall include all methods of solicitation, including but not limited to spoken, written, or printed words, or by other means of communication, including but not limited to bodily gestures.
Public area shall mean an area to which the public or a substantial group of persons has access, including, but not limited to, streets, highways, roadways (including shoulders and medians), bridges, the area above and below any bridge, sidewalks, alleys, parking lots and decks, plazas, parks, public green space areas, playgrounds, schools, transportation facilities, within a public-transportation vehicle, an area owned in whole or in part by, operated by, for, or under the custody and control of Glynn County, Georgia, and any other property where public gatherings occur on a regular basis, and any other property where public meetings are conducted.
Outdoor dining area shall mean an outdoor dining area of a restaurant or other establishment serving food or drink for immediate consumption.
Charitable organization means a bona fide philanthropic, patriotic, or eleemosynary corporation, partnership, limited liability company, association, joint-stock company, trust, unincorporated organization or individual who engages in solicitation exclusively for charitable purposes from the general public.
Non-profit organization means a corporation, partnership, limited liability company, association, joint-stock company, trust, unincorporated organization or individual which is certified as exempt from payment of United States Income Taxes by the Internal Revenue Service, or any "educational institution" as defined in O.C.G.A. § 20-1-10.
(Ord. No. O-2024-03, § II, 3/21/2024)
1252:
Representatives or agents of Non-Profit Organizations and Charitable Organizations, which intend to engage in solicitation, shall be treated as exempt from the requirements of this Article, provided that the Non-Profit Organization or Charitable Organization first supplies proof of its exempt status to the Glynn County Finance Department, such as articles of incorporation from the Secretary of State showing non-profit status, a 501(c) letter from the Internal Revenue Service, a Georgia state tax exemption, or other comparable confirmation of exempt status. Upon receipt of such proof, the Glynn County Finance Department will issue credentials to such Non-Profit Organizations and Charitable Organizations that may be copied and disseminated to their field representatives. Representatives or agents of Non-Profit Organizations and Charitable Organizations must, at all times engaging in solicitation, maintain upon their person a copy of said credentials and produce said credentials upon demand of any person.
(Ord. No. O-2024-03, § II, 3/21/2024)
1253:
It shall be unlawful for any person within the unincorporated areas of the Glynn County, Georgia, to commit any of the following acts:
(a) No person shall solicit for money or other thing of value within any public area of the unincorporated areas of the Glynn County, Georgia.
(b) No person shall solicit on private property without first having obtained the permission of the owner or other person legally in possession of the property.
(c) No person shall solicit on private property if the owner or other person legally in possession of the property has notified the person, by signage or otherwise, that they are not allowed to solicit on the property.
(d) No person shall solicit within thirty (30) feet of any automated teller machine or any bank, financial institution, or check-cashing facility.
(e) No person shall solicit while under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance, as defined by Georgia or federal law.
(f) No person shall solicit within ten (10) feet of the entrance or exit of a building.
(g) No person shall solicit within thirty (30) feet of an outdoor dining area.
(h) No person shall solicit an operator or passenger of a motor vehicle while such person is operating or occupying a motor vehicle.
(Ord. No. O-2024-03, § II, 3/21/2024)
